requirements.text: One small closable PETG enclosure accepts interchangeable separately printed TPU liners and a loose metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests one small PETG exterior, closable, with TPU inserts and space to shake a stock metal nut.

questions.criterion: Cup/pad clear the existing shell, each other and installation travel; expanded flat cavity admits a moving 12 mm nut proxy.
Printed pair swaps, seats and stays retained during shaking.

requirements.text: The floor, ceiling and all four interior walls have TPU damping coverage.

provenance.statement: User explicitly requires damping on the bottom, top, and all four walls.

questions.criterion: Six continuous flat skins retain the declared 0.6 mm thickness.
Printed liner remains intact, including shell-side features.

requirements.text: All object-contact interior faces are flat; damping structures are inside the liner.

provenance.statement: User clarification: the interior needs to be flat for the objects, while the liner may have structures inside.

questions.criterion: The expanded cubic shaking cavity is free of protrusions.

requirements.text: Several permanently labeled CAD-defined internal damping configurations can be printed together.

provenance.statement: User asks for labeled variants, explicit CAD structures rather than infill, and a batch print; additional variants are welcome.

questions.criterion: Air channels and declared chevron or straight-rib material remain behind all six faces.
Both parts bear matching large bold recessed I30/I22/I10 labels, at least 8 mm actual capital height, with material above the recess.
Labels remain readable, thin skins and web bridges print intact.
Printed core channels remain separated and open.

requirements.text: Use research to inform a reusable damping experiment and compare variants by shaking the same metal nut.

provenance.statement: User requests research on effective damping structures and plans to report which liner performs best.

questions.criterion: Same-shell/nut comparison includes shake intensity and axis; larger cavity is acknowledged.
User reports relative quietness of I22/I30/I10.

requirements.text: Prioritize maximum quietness in a thin liner and recommend a focused print batch with a solid control and the most promising candidates.

provenance.statement: User follow-up: maximize quietness while keeping it thin; provide a STEP set focused on more confident candidates and retain control A.

questions.criterion: One batch contains exactly three I-derived pairs at 3.0, 2.2 and 1.0 mm, 25/45/75 percent thinner than approved I.
User compares against approved 4 mm I and finds an acceptable thickness/quietness tradeoff.

requirements.text: Thinner follow-up liners retain both continuous inner and outer TPU skins for stable printing.

provenance.statement: User reports I10 shell-side print damage, says both walls are needed, and requests one or two significantly thinner stable variants; slicer changes are allowed.

questions.criterion: Declared CAD architecture retains a continuous outer backing and inner skin.

evidence.summary: Shell-side regions broken in print; some damping, I22 better. User suspects absent outer skin. Exact print settings/artifacts unknown.
User reports broken shell-side regions; I10 is rejected for use. Absent outer skin is a suspected cause.
Open-backed I10 lacks the now-required outer skin.

decisions.text: Reuse outer 34 mm cup and existing shell; expand cavity instead of adding rigid fillers. I22 retains 0.9 mm chevrons; I10 uses a 0.6 mm contact skin over 0.4 mm open gap with 1.2 mm support ribs, bed frames and local label panels.

hypotheses.text: Reduced core stroke may cause bottoming; shorter webs can stiffen despite thinner sections. Original I approval does not transfer.

directives.text: Preserve approved I; deliver three much thinner derivatives for printing.

source.statement: User reports I much more damping, explicitly approves it, and requests two or three much thinner I variants.
